overview: This Senate resolution marks one year since the wildfires that broke out in Los Angeles County and nearby counties on January 7, 2025. It notes that the fires, including the Palisades and Eaton fires, killed 31 people, destroyed more than 16,000 structures and displaced over 200,000 people, making them among the costliest natural disasters in U.S. history. The resolution honors those who died, praises the firefighters and first responders from across the country and abroad who fought the fires, and states the Senate's commitment to helping the affected communities rebuild. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on January 8, 2026.
for: Supporters say it honors the victims and first responders and signals continued attention to communities still rebuilding.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and doesn't change any law or provide new spending for recovery.
